Th is petition coming on for hearing this day, th e court passed the
following:
 Order

The present petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India has been directed against the order dated 03.02.2020 passed in appeal No.29/18-19 by Additional Commissioner, Gwalior Division, Gwalior, wherein the order dated 28.09.2018 passed by Sub Divisional Officer in first appeal No.12/15-16 was challenged and while dismissing the second appeal the order of first appeal was affirmed, wherein the order dated 10.09.2012 passed by Tehsildar on an application under Section 178 of M.P. Land Revenue Code for partition moved by the present respondents was allowed and partition was directed to be carried out of land bearing survey Nos.1041, 1509, 1510, 1511, 1514,
1841, 1843, 1844, 1845, 1846, 1847, 1848, 1849, 1850, 1851, 1852, 1853, 1854, 1855, 1856, 1857,
1858, 1859, 1861, 1866, 1867, 1868, 1869, 1870, 1871 and 2302 situated at village Kurthara, District Datia admeasuring 7.34 hectares.
Brief facts of the case are that the present respondents herein had filed an application under Section 178 of M.P.L.R.C. for partition of the joint holdings of survey numbers as mentioned above.

In the application, it was wrongly mentioned that total area of joint holdings was 7.34 hectares, whereas the area of joint holdings remaining was only 6.64 hectares as 0.7 hectare was acquired by the State for the purpose of irrigation.
In the application preferred by the present respondents though the names of the petitioners were mentioned but the address mentioned therein was only Datia.

After registering the case for the partition by Tehsildar notices were directed to be issued but instead of serving the present petitioners personally the notices were affixed on a house, though from the copies of the aforesaid notices, it is not reflected whether the said notices were affixed on the original houses of the present petitioners.

Treating the said affixture of notices to be a proper service on the present petitioners, the Tehsildar proceeded with the matter and on the basis of Fard Batwara prepared by the Revenue Inspector allowed the said application and passed the order dated 10.09.2012 for partition.

2

Aggrieved by the said order passed by Tehsildar dated 10.09.2012 an appeal was preferred before the Sub Divisional Officer and since the said appeal was barred by limitation was accompanied with the application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
The Sub Divisional Officer rejected the said application under Section 5 of Limitation Act vide order dated 06.09.2017 and consequently also dismissed the appeal.
Against the said order of dismissal of the application under Section 5 of Limitation Act, the present petitioners had preferred a second appeal before the Additional Commissioner.
Learned Additional Commissioner

after considering the aspect that notices were not at all issued to the present petitioners and no opportunity of hearing was granted to them by Tehsildar and as the said order was against the principles of natural justice and was not within the knowledge of present petitioners, application under Section 5 of Limitation Act has wrongly been rejected by the Sub Divisional Officer and, therefore, the matter was remanded back to the Sub Divisional Officer after condoning the delay in preferring the appeal, to decide the first appeal on its own merits.
After remand the Sub Divisional Officer issued notices to the parties and after giving opportunity of hearing to both the parties decided the said appeal on merits but Sub Divisional Officer did not consider the basic ground which was raised by the present petitioners with regard to non grant of opportunity of hearing by Tehsildar on the ground of non-service of notices upon the petitioners/appellants, went on to decide the appeal on merits holding that the notices were published by the Tehsildar for only 6.64 hectares for partition and also the Fard Batwara prepared by the Patwari was with regard to 6.64 hectares and even the present report of the Patwari which was received after the remand found the parties to be in possession as per the partition which has taken place and since 0.70 hectares of land had been acquired, the compensation of which has been received by the present petitioners/appellants and as the said land could not be reduced in the revenue records for which appellants have even not given any explanation, the partition order which has been passed by the Tehsildar could not be faulted with.

The said order dated 28.09.2018 passed by Sub Divisional Officer after remand was again challenged by the present petitioners before the Additional Commissioner and learned Additional Commissioner ignoring its findings passed in earlier order dated 10.09.2012 affirmed the order of Sub Divisional Officer.
Hence, the present petition.

Shri N.K. Gupta, learned senior counsel with Shri YPS Rathore, learned counsel for the petitioner has vehemently argued that both the Courts i.e. Sub Divisional Officer as well as Additional Commissioner had misdirected itself in not considering that the order passed by Tehsildar was per se illegal since it was passed in absence of present petitioners, as admittedly, notices issued by Tehsildar were not served upon the present petitioners which could be reflected from the very endorsement made on the notices which were submitted by the officer who had served the said notices, wherein on each and every notice it was mentioned that since the parties could not be found the notices have been affixed on some open place on their house.

Further reliance was placed on the Rules of Procedure of Revenue Officers and Revenue Courts for issuance of summons as provided under Scheduled I framed under Section 258(2-a)(2-c) of M.P.
Rambabu vs Pradeep on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126695310/
3 Land Revenue Code, wherein Rule 4 was referred to which provides for delivery of summons to a person summoned personally or to his recognised agent and Rule 5 which provides that where the person summoned cannot be found and has no recognised agent, service may be made on any adult male member of the family of the person summoned, who is residing with him and as per Rule 6,
where the serving officer delivers or tenders a copy of the summons to the person summoned personally or to his recognised agent or other person on his behalf, he shall require the signature of the person, to whom the copy is delivered or tendered to an acknowledgement of service endorsed on the original summons and if such a person is not found personally neither agent of such person is found, then as provided under Rule 7, it should be affixed at the last known place of residence of the person summoned or at some place of public resort in such village and lastly as per Rule 8, where a copy of the summons is affixed as provided in Rule 7, the serving Officer shall return the original copy of the summons to the Court from which it was issued, with a report endorsed thereon or annexed thereto stating that he has affixed the copy, the circumstances under which he did so and the name and the address of the person in whose presence the copy was affixed and where the copy is affixed at the last known place of residence of the person summoned, the report shall also contain the name and address of the person, if any, by whom the house was identified and since the procedure provided under these rules were not adhered to by the serving officer, the service on the present petitioners could not be deemed to be effected, therefore, the very order passed by Tehsildar was per se illegal and deserves to be set aside.

It was further argued that the entire process which has been followed by Tehsildar since was not sustainable and same has not been considered by the first and second appellate authority, both the orders suffers from patent illegality and, therefore, it was prayed that the petition deserves to be allowed and the orders impugned are required to be set aside and the matter deserves to be relegated back to Tehsildar for carrying out the procedure of partition afresh in accordance with law.
Per contra, Shri J.P. Kushwah, learned counsel appearing for the respondents contends that no illegality has been committed by the Courts below in passing the order as the present petitioners have not approached the authorities with clean hands.

It was further contended that out of total survey numbers i.e. 7.34 hectares, 0.07 hectare of land was already acquired by State Government for irrigation purposes and compensation of such acquisition was already received by the present petitioners but this fact has not been disclosed by the petitioners while preferring the appeal.

It was further argued that after remand the learned Sub Divisional Officer had found on procuring fresh report from Patwari with regard to the holdings of the land by the parties that the petitioners and the respondents were in occupation of the respective holdings as per the terms of the partition and, therefore, the contentions of the petitioners that no opportunity of hearing was granted to them or partition was asked for a wrong area is baseless and devoid of any substance.

It was lastly argued that the learned Additional Commissioner also considered the aforesaid fact that the parties are in occupation of their respective holdings as per the terms of the partition, the second appeal preferred by the present petitioners was held to be baseless and illegal, thus, it was prayed that the present petition being devoid of any substance deserves to be dismissed.

4
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

The basic challenge by the present petitioners was to the orders passed by the Sub Divisional Officer passed in first appeal dated 28.09.2018 and by the Additional Commissioner in second appeal dated 03.02.2020 contending them to be illegal on the ground that both the Authorities had not considered that the order passed by Tehsildar dated 10.09.2012 in the partition proceedings was vitiated because the petitioners herein were not given any opportunity of hearing, as the notices which were issued by Tehsildar were never served upon them and since the order passed by Tehsildar dated 10.09.2012 was dehors the principle of natural justice, the same was not sustainable.

From bare perusal of the orders passed by Sub Divisional Officer as well as Additional Commissioner, this fact is very much evident that the contention of the petitioners as mentioned above were not at all considered.

The service of notices on the petitioners in the proceedings initiated by Tehsildar on an application under Section 178 of M.P. Land Revenue Code for partition moved at the behest of respondents whether was affected or could have been deemed, was a question, which both the Courts have ignored.

This Court is in agreement with the contentions made by learned senior counsel that the Rules of Procedure of Revenue Officers and Revenue Courts for issuance of summons as provided under Scheduled I framed under Section 258(2-a)(2-c) of M.P. Land Revenue Code were not adhered to by Tehsildar.

entities.text: Rules of Procedure of Revenue Officers and Revenue Courts
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The serving officer has not mentioned that when the petitioners were not found at their residence, it had tried to effect the service on any adult member of the family, further there is also no mention of the fact that when he could not serve the notices either on the petitioners or on adult male member of the family, therefore, he had affixed the said notices on some conspicuous place of residence of the petitioners, or some other place which was visible to all the villagers as provided under the Rules, rather where the notices were affixed is not known and also in whose presence the said notices had been affixed is also not mentioned, thus, according to this Court it could be said with certainty that the notices were not at all served upon the petitioners.

In absence of service of notices on the petitioners of the proceedings which were conducted by the Tehsildar, the entire proceedings as well as order passed by Tehsildar according to this Court stands vitiated and cannot be sustained.
Accordingly, the said order deserves to be set aside.

Since the aspect of service of notice on petitioners in proceedings of partition before Tehsildar has not been considered by first appellate Court i.e. Sub Divisional Officer and the Additional Commissioner i.e.
second appellate authority, both the orders also suffers from illegality and accordingly cannot be sustained.

Thus, the order dated 03.02.2020 passed by Additional Commissioner, Gwalior Division, Gwalior,
order dated 28.09.2018 passed by Sub Divisional Officer and the order dated 10.09.2012 passed by Tehsildar are hereby set aside.

As a natural coronary, the matter is remanded back to the Tehsildar for taking afresh decision on the application preferred by the present respondents under Section 178 of M.P. Land Revenue Code after giving opportunity of hearing to all the interested parties.
Parties are directed to remain present before Tehsildar on 05th September, 2023.

5
With the aforesaid, the petition stands allowed and disposed of.
